subcategory: education regulation — private schools, home education
name: Nova Scotia — private schools and home education
description: Nova Scotia private schools are not publicly funded (except partial tuition support at designated special-education private schools). The province defines a private school as one with a curriculum comparable to the public schools (Education Act 2018, ss.85–87) and publishes a list of private schools recognized to grant the Nova Scotia High School Leaving Certificate. Home education requires an annual registration form received by 20 September; it is unfunded, the Minister may terminate a programme that does not meet the Act, and the Home Schooling division awards no credits or diplomas.

attributes.legal_term: Private school (Education Act, S.N.S. 2018, c.1, ss.85–87)
attributes.funding: None, except the Tuition Support Program at Designated Special Education Private Schools (DESPS).
attributes.curriculum: 'A curriculum comparable to that provided by the public schools' (ednet.ns.ca).
attributes.register: Open data: Recognized Private Schools Granting the NS High School Leaving Certificate (modified 2026-10-14). Current rows include Armbrae Academy, Halifax Grammar School, King's-Edgehill School, Sacred Heart School of Halifax, Shambhala School, Class Afloat (West Island College International), DEVI International Boarding School, Maritime Muslim Academy and three designated special-education schools (Bridgeway Academy ×2, Churchill Academy, Landmark East). No public list of private elementary-only schools was found.
attributes.diploma: Only recognized private schools on that list grant the NS High School Leaving Certificate.
attributes.home_education: Annual Registration Form for Home Schooling due 20 September (2026-27 form published); unfunded; Minister may terminate a programme on evidence it does not meet the Act or the child is not progressing (s.84); no credits or graduation certificate from the division; a home-educated child may take board courses with board approval.
